_comment: Native `--format json` baseline digest for the axilog-cli facade regression guard (M17 Task 3). See facade_identity.rs for the regeneration procedure. Regenerated for the healing-extension roster change: `blocks.healing` gained an `extension` descriptor (version/revision/signature, decoded from the addon's registration row) and every `blocks.healing.by_entity` row gained `runs_extension` — GW2EI's `RunningExtension` roster, which the native format previously did not carry at all, leaving EI-shaped consumers unable to tell 'this player's healing numbers are complete' from 'partial, relayed by a peer'. Both are intentional new fields, so byteLength grew by 1563 from the pre-roster baseline. Re-digested (byteLength unchanged) for the 1.2.0 version bump: the document embeds `axilog.version`, so every release bump moves this digest by exactly that string. Determinism verified at each regeneration: two independent captures produced byte-identical output and identical sha256 digests. Regenerated for `blocks.self_effects`: the squad-side counterpart to `blocks.conditions`, carrying per-(squad player, effect) uptime and a fused stack timeline for the 14 conditions plus Stun (872) and Daze (833). It is a new opt-in block gated on the existing `--timeseries` flag, which `--all` turns on, so byteLength grew by 248477. Determinism verified: two independent captures of the new output were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Re-digested for the `blocks.self_effects` all-zero drop-rule fix: the pass previously emitted a row for a zero-length buff application, whose fused timeline is `[[0, 0], [t, 0]]` -- two entries, so it slipped past the old `len() < 2` guard -- carrying no information, and in one case an `avg_stacks: 0.0` the schema's own convention says should be omitted rather than reported. The guard now tests for a nonzero stack value, dropping exactly those rows: 345 self_effects rows became 343 (entity 22 buff 738 and entity 34 buff 26766 removed), so byteLength shrank by 521. Elite Insights omits such a buff from `buffUptimes` entirely, and the EI equality oracle is unchanged by this (476 cells, worst duration 0.000500pp, worst intensity 0.000497rel, before and after) because it never compared those keys. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Re-digested (byteLength unchanged at 8499154) for the 1.3.0 version bump: the document embeds `axilog.version`, so every release bump moves this digest by exactly that string. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Re-digested for the GW2 API skill-name fallback: `skill_icons` gained a second generated table, `SKILL_NAMES` (4,610 of the API's 4,702 skills), and `skill_map::resolve_name` now consults it before falling back to the `"Skill <id>"` placeholder — arcdps writes no display name for a skill its client had not cached, which left 61 of this fixture's catalog entries reading `"Skill 14404"` where the skill is Signet of Might. The change is purely additive: it ranks BELOW the log's own table, so it can only displace the placeholder. Machine-diffed leaf by leaf against the 1.3.0 baseline: exactly 61 leaves moved, every one of them a `catalogs.skills.*.name`, every one from a placeholder to a real GW2 name and none in the other direction. byteLength grew by 203. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Regenerated for `blocks.squad_buffs`: squad-side uptime for every buff that is neither one of the 12 boons nor a condition/control effect — sigils, relics, food, utilities, auras, signets, trait buffs. Elite Insights keeps that whole population in the same `buffUptimes` array as the boons; this project split it by family and the tail previously had no home at all, which is why axibridge's Special Buffs and Sigil/Relic Uptime sections rendered empty. Unlike `blocks.self_effects` this block is ALWAYS-ON: it emits uptime only, at the cost `blocks.boons`' own always-on half already carries. Machine-diffed leaf by leaf against the 1.3.0 skill-name baseline: purely additive — 1,012 new `blocks.squad_buffs.by_entity` leaves across 38 entities, 162 new reference-scoped `catalogs.buffs` entries, and one changed leaf (`coverage.squad_buffs`, `not_computed` -> `present`). Nothing removed, nothing else changed; the pre-block capture was byte-identical to the previous baseline apart from the 35-byte `coverage.squad_buffs` key the new `BlockName` variant adds. byteLength grew by 117397. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Re-digested (byteLength unchanged at 8616754) for the 1.4.0 version bump: the document embeds `axilog.version`, so every release bump moves this digest by exactly that string. Proven rather than assumed this time -- the new capture contains exactly ONE occurrence of "1.4.0", and substituting "1.3.0" back for it reproduces the previous baseline's digest (538e5b7e...) byte for byte, so nothing else in the document moved. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Regenerated for the post-SotO elite-spec ids 77/78/79 (Antiquary/Galeshot/Conduit): the profession table stopped at 81 with those three holes, and an unmapped id degrades to the BASE profession, so axibridge rendered a Conduit as a plain “Revenant” (reported from a live raid night). Machine-diffed leaf by leaf against the 1.4.0 baseline: 206,050 leaves on both sides, nothing added, nothing removed, exactly FIVE changed leaves — entities 47 (Thief/77 → Antiquary) and 48/55/63/70 (Revenant/79 → Conduit), each from "" to a name and none in the other direction. byteLength grew by exactly 37, which is len("Antiquary") + 4×len("Conduit"). This fixture carries no Ranger/78 agent, so Galeshot does not appear here; it is covered by axibridge’s testdata/20260117-175120.zevtc and by the unit test. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests, and the pre-change build reproduced the previous baseline digest (97e24d0c…) byte for byte. Re-digested (byteLength unchanged at 8616791) for the 1.4.1 version bump: the document embeds `axilog.version`, so every release bump moves this digest by exactly that string. Proven rather than assumed: the new capture contains exactly ONE occurrence of "1.4.1", and substituting "1.4.0" back for it reproduces the pre-bump digest (1cb93878…) byte for byte, so nothing else in the document moved. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests. Re-digested (byteLength unchanged at 8616791) for the 1.5.0 version bump: the document embeds `axilog.version`, so every release bump moves this digest by exactly that string. Proven rather than assumed: the new capture contains exactly ONE occurrence of "1.5.0", and substituting "1.4.1" back for it reproduces the pre-bump digest (a1f0842d…) byte for byte. That substitution also settles the question this release actually raises — v1.5.0 adds PvE encounter identification, including four new optional `encounter` keys (`encounter_name`, `trigger_id`, `sub_category`, `success`) — by showing that NONE of them reach this document: they are `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` and this fixture is a WvW log, whose `pve` identity is `None` by construction. Determinism verified: two independent captures were byte-identical with identical sha256 digests.
